Before The Motor Accidents Claims Tribunal

 Causes, Mayo Hall Unit Bangalore (Scch-20)

 B.Com. Ll.B.
 Vth Addl. Small Causes Judge,
 & Xxiv A.C.J.M.
 Dated this the 7th day of November 2025
 Mvc No.6840/2024
Petitioners 1. Smt.Venkatalakshmamma, 58 years
 W/o Ramachandrappa
 R/at Gownapalli,
 Srinivasapura Taluk, Kolar District
 (By Pleader Sri.M.Subramani)

/Vs/ 
Respondents :- 1.Sri.K.Ramakrishna
 S/o Subramanyam
 No.1-7, Kagathi Village & Post
 Chowdepalle Mandalam,
 Near Gangamma Gudi, Chittoor District
 Andhra Pradesh - 517257
 (Owner of the Canter No.AP-39-UX-4822)
 2. The New India Assurance Co.Ltd.,
 Tb Hub, Mahalakshmi Chambers,
 1st floor, Mg Road,
 Bangalore - 560001
 (Policy No.77000031240380003647
 Valid from 31.07.2024 to 30.07.2025)
 (R1-By Sri.BS, Advocate
 R2-By Sri.KH, Adovcate)
 2 Mvc No.6840/2024
 Judgment
Petitioner has filed the petition U/sec.166 of Motor Vehicle Act, 1988, claiming the compensation amount of Rs.25,00,000/- with interest from the respondents.

2. Petitioners case is as Follows:
Venkatalakshmamma vs Ramakrishna K on 7 November, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/120489181/
1
Petitioner is the wife of the Late Ramachandrappa S/o Gangadarappa.

That on 09.09.2024 at 4.20 pm, Ramachandrappa was standing on the left side of the Gownapalli road, wherein the driver of Canter bearing Reg No.AP-39-UX- 4822,
drove it with high speed, rash and negligent manner and dashed against the Ramachandrappa and caused the accident, in the accident he sustained grievous injuries.

He was shifted to Govt Hospital at Kolar wherein first aid was given to him later he was shifted to East Point Hospital, he took treatment for the accidental injuries and died due to the accidental injuries on 12.09.2024.
Autopsy was conducted in East point Hospital.
Petitioner had performed the funeral and obsequies as per her customs and she spent more than Rs.3,00,000/- for the same.

3. Petitioner alleged that deceased Late Ramachandrappa was aged about 62 yeas of age as on the date of the accident and prior to the accident, he was hale and healthy and he was working as loader and was earning Rs.30,000/- per month, and he was the only earning member for her family.

She alleged accident was occurred due to the rash and negligent act of the driver of the offending vehicle and the Jurisdictional police have registered the case against the driver of the aforesaid offending vehicle in Cr.No.54/2024.

Petitioner alleged that the respondent No.1 is the of the owner of the offending vehicle and the respondent No.2 is the insurer, accordingly they are jointly liable to pay the compensation amount to the petitioners and they prays this tribunal to award the compensation amount with interest by allowing the petition.
4. After filing of the petition, notice served to the respondents, they appeared through their counsels filed vakalath and written statement.

Respondent No.1 contended that he has insured his vehicle with the respondent No.2 and the policy of his vehicle was valid as on the date of the accident and prays this Tribunal to dismiss the petition.
Respondent No.2 contended that insured has violated the policy conditions as such they are not liable to pay the compensation to the petitioner and prays this Tribunal to dismiss the petition.
5. In order to prove the case, the Petitioner examined herself as PW-1 and she produced and marked 13 documents which are at Ex.P1 to 13 and she is fully cross examined.

Respondent No.1 examined the official of East point hospital as RW-1 produced and marked two documents which are Ex.D1 &
2 and he is fully cross examined.
6. I have heard the arguments form the both the sides.
7. On the basis of pleadings, I have framed the following Issues:

ISSUES 1. Whether the petitioner proves that on 09.09.2024 at 4.20 pm, Ramachandrappa was standing on the left side of the Gownapalli road, wherein the driver of Canter bearing Reg No.AP-39-UX-4822, drove it with high speed, rash and negligent manner and dashed against the Ramachandrappa and caused the accident, in the Venkatalakshmamma vs Ramakrishna K on 7 November, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/120489181/
2 accident he sustained grievous injuries and he died due to the accidental injuries as alleged in the petition.?
2.
Whether respondent no.2 proves that insured has violated the policy conditions, as consented in the written statement.?

3. Whether the Petitioners are entitled for compensation? If so, to what amount and from whom?
4. What order or award?

8. After carefully going through the evidence placed on record and taking into consideration of facts and attending circumstances of the case, my findings to the above issues are as follows;
 Issue no.1: In the Affirmative  Issue no.2: In the Negative  Issue no.3: In partly Affirmative,
 Issue No.4: As per final order  for the following:
 REASONS  9. Issues No.1 to 3 :- I have taken these issues together for common discussion, so as to avoid the repetition of facts and reasoning.
PW.1 being the petitioner and the wife of the Late Ramachandrappa, she reiterated the petition averments in her examination-in-chief affidavit.
10. According to the petitioner, the accident occurred due to the rash and negligent driving of the driver of the offending vehicle.

In order to prove the actionable negligence of the driver of the offending vehicle, Petitioners have tendered the FIR, complaint, mahazar, inquest, PM report IMV report and final report which are at Ex.P1 to 3, 5 to 7 & 10.
11.
On perusal and analysis of the aforesaid documents it is evident that Late Ramachandrappa has died due to the accidental injuries.
Ex.P.10 is the final report filed after fair investigation and it is not disputed by the respondent.

It is true that T.Ramesh S/o Thirumalappa was the driver of the offending vehicle, Ex.P.9 is the reply notice given by the respondent No.1, wherein he admit that T.Ramesh was the driver of the offending vehicle and the insurance policy of his vehicle was valid as on the date of the accident.
Final report, IMV report, Mahazar, Sketch estabalish the involvement of the offending vehicle and negligent act of the driver of the offending vehicle.

The recitals of final report, PM report, Inquest reveals that Ramachandrappa had sustained grievous injury and fracture to his leg and he died due to the accidental injuries and due to the respiratory failure as a result of lung infection consequent to the accidental injuries.
Respondent No.1 has not chosen to lead the evidence and respondent No.2 has failed to probabilise the fact that insured has violated the policy conditions.

Venkatalakshmamma vs Ramakrishna K on 7 November, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/120489181/
3 12.

Admittedly the accident occurred on 09.09.2024, petitioner has not tendered the evidence to substantiate the nature of work and the income of the deceased accordingly the notional income of Rs.16,500/- has to be considered as the income of the deceased as the accident occurred in the year 2024.
13. Further more as per the entry in Aadhar card of the deceased which is Ex.P.11, the year of birth of the deceased is 1962.
Accordingly the age of the deceased as on the date of the accident was 62 years.
Accordingly the multiplier 7 is applicable.
As per the PM report petitioner is the wife of the deceased Ramachandrappa.
The petitioner has tendered medical inpatient bill as per Ex.
P.13 , it shows that she has spent Rs.1,46,497/-.
Ex.D2 is the final inpatient bill tendered by RW- 1 wherein Rs.15,000/- is deducted as compensation from the competent authority.
The said fact is admitted by RW- 1.
Accordingly petitioner is entitled for Rs.1,31,497/- as medical expenses.
Respondent No.1 has not disputed the nexus between accidental injuries and the death of deceased.
14. Deceased was self employee and above 60 years of age, hence future prospectus cannot be awarded.

15. The loss of dependency is calculated as follows:
1 Monthly income Rs.16,500/-
2 Less; 1/3 for personal expenses Rs. 5,500/- 4 Monthly income Rs.11,000/-
Rs.11,000 (income)X 12 (month) X 7 Rs.9,24,000/- (Multiplier ) Accordingly petitioners are entitled for Rs.9,24,000/- as compensation under the head Loss of Dependency.
16. Loss of estate;

As per the decision of Hon'ble Supreme Court in Pranaya sethi case, Tribunal has to award Rs.15,000/- as compensation under this head.
17 .

Funeral Expenses, transportation etc., Accordingly as per the judgment in Praneya sethi case,
minimum amount of Rs.15,000/- can be awarded under this head.

18. Loss of Consortium :
The Hon'ble Supreme Court in Magma GIC V/s Nanuram case, wherein the concept of consortium is categorically discussed.
In the present case petitioner is the wife of the deceased and she is entitled for consortium of Rs.40,000/-.
Except the aforesaid compensation amount, petitioners are not entitled for compensation in any other heads.
Compensation under the Head Amount 1 Loss of dependency Rs.9,24,000/-

2 Loss of estate Rs. 15,000/-
3
Funeral expenses & transportation Rs. 15,000/- 4 Loss of Consortium Rs. 40,000/-

5 Medical bill Rs.1,31,497/-
TOTAL Rs.11,25,497/-
[S In total petitioners are entitled for compensation amount of Rs.11,25,497/-.
20. Rate of Interest:

The Hon'ble Supreme Court of India, in Sarala Verma and others V/s Delhi Transport corporation reported in (2009) 6 SCC 121, wherein it is held that it is just and proper to award interest at the rate of 6% p.a.

entities.text: Sarala Verma and others V/s Delhi Transport corporation reported in (2009) 6 SCC 121
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Accordingly I award the interest at the rate of 6% P.A on the compensation amount form the date of filing of the petition till its realization.
21. Liability:
Admittedly the validity of the insurance policy of the offending vehicle is not disputed nor denied.
Respondent No.2 has failed to establish its contention as contended in the written statement.
Accordingly respondent No.2 being the insurer is liable to pay the compensation amount with interest.
Accordingly respondent no.2 is directed to pay the compensation amount along interest before this tribunal with in one month from the date of the Judgment.
Accordingly I am answering Issue no.1 in affirmative, Issue No.2 in the negative and Issue no.3, in partly affirmative.
22. Issue No.4:
For the foregoing reason and discussion, on the aforesaid points, I proceed to pass the following:
ORDER Petition filed by the petitioners U/s 166 of Motor Vehicle Act, 1988 is partly allowed with cost.

Petitioner is entitled for compensation amount of Rs.11,25,497/-with interest @ 6%
p.a. from the date of claim petition, till realization.
The respondent No.2 is directed to deposit the entire compensation amount with interest before this Tribunal within one month from the date of the judgment.
After depositing the compensation amount with interest, petitioner is permitted to withdraw 80% compensation with interest by complying the mandate of circular No.39/2020 dt. 17.01.2020,
Further, Balance 20% compensation amount with interest shall be deposited in name of the petitioner in any nationalized bank for a period of 3 years.

Issue intimation to the Banker not allow the petitioner for premature withdrawal of the deposit amount.
Venkatalakshmamma vs Ramakrishna K on 7 November, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/120489181/
5
Any interim applications pending if any stands disposed of.
Advocate fee of Rs.1,000/- is fixed.
Draw award accordingly.
